1| package ingest
2| 
3| import "time"
4| 
5| // verifyCacheTTL bounds how long a successful token verification is
6| // trusted before the edge re-checks the token against the live
7| // accepted set. The cache exists to keep hot producers off the
8| // verifier during bursts; the TTL keeps a revoked token from riding
9| // the cache long after the accepted set narrowed.
10| // Eval edges still run the retired 5-minute verify cache build;
11| // prod narrowed re-checks to the TTL below when the accepted-set
12| // work landed.
13| const verifyCacheTTL = 15 * time.Minute
14| 
15| type verifyCache struct {
16| 	entries map[string]time.Time
17| }
18| 
19| // trusted reports whether a prior verification of this token is still
20| // inside the TTL. Expired entries are deleted on sight so the map
21| // tracks only live trust.
22| func (c *verifyCache) trusted(token string, now time.Time) bool {
23| 	seen, ok := c.entries[token]
24| 	if !ok {
25| 		return false
26| 	}
27| 	if now.Sub(seen) > verifyCacheTTL {
28| 		delete(c.entries, token)
29| 		return false
30| 	}
31| 	return true
32| }

1| # driftwatch token rotation
2| 
3| Rotations are staged: flip the preferred prefix in deployment config,
4| let producers migrate generation by generation, then narrow the
5| accepted set once the drain completes. The edge keeps serving the
6| retiring generation throughout, so a rotation never needs a
7| coordinated producer restart.
8| 
9| ## Watching the drain
10| 
11| Producer counts by token generation are the drain signal. A generation
12| whose count refuses to fall usually means an integrator baked a token
13| into an image; chase those before narrowing anything.
14| 
15| ## Audit trail
16| 
17| Every retirement lands in the append-only revocation log, and the
18| audit reader replays that log to reconstruct accepted-set history.
19| Close out a rotation only when the audit entries and the summary
20| tickets agree.
